messages:
Alex M.: quick handoff — I'm switching primary to Ben in ~10m. I'm in the bridge for the next 5, will pass context. :wave:
Alex M.: current customer-impacting alert is the model-queue lag (see incidentbot below). No user-facing errors yet but increased tail latency for embeddings writes.
Alex M.: Access checklist before I drop: PD primary toggle to Ben (Ben C.), Grafana org role 'oncall-view' for Ben, AWS assume-role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-oncall for grafana logs & lambda restart, and jumpbox sudo for any host-level fixes.
Ben C.: got it. I already have PD secondary but not primary. Priya, can you confirm PD primary transfer won't break the auto-escalation?
Priya S.: PD handover is safe — we use the rotation rule. I'll promote Ben and reassign session policies. Also granting Ben the AWS role now (JIT ticket #4567).
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert created: model-queue-lag - high-kafka-lag on embeddings-pipeline. Severity: P2. Affected customers: 2 high-usage tenants (tenant-42, tenant-77). Link: https://go.redwood/incidents/3301234567
Alex M.: quick mitigation steps in runbook: https://go.redwood/runbooks/oncall-queue-lag — start with tailing the consumer group, then check autoscaler and recent deploys. If autoscaler is saturated, consider manual scale: `kubectl scale deployment embeddings-consumer --replicas=6 -n prod`.
Ben C.: copying commands. I don't have prod kube creds from this laptop — I can use the jumpbox if sudo works. Priya, JIT ETA?
Priya S.: JIT role created, expires in 45m. I added Ben to sudoers on the jumpbox for the session. Also added Grafana: team 'oncall' has dashboard write for short-term annotations.
Alex M.: note: grafana link for latency dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/latency/embeddings. If you need logs, use `awslogs` on the jumpbox: `aws logs tail /aws/lambda/emb-consumer --follow --profile oncall`
SRE Oncall: if autoscaler is saturated, check the cluster's target group and spot capacity — last two scale events failed due to insufficient spot offers in us-west-2. Fallback: switch consumer nodepool to on-demand pool `nodepool=oncall-on-demand` and force scale.
Ben C.: doing a quick pre-check: PD primary transfer in progress... done. Grafana role confirmed. AWS role assumed: success.
Alex M.: I'll post a short context dump before I leave the bridge: recent deploy at 20:13 changed commit 5f3a2 -> tokenizer mem tweak. Might've increased memory churn in consumers. Start with rolling restart of consumer pods if memory climbs. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/embeddings-consumer -n prod`.
Ben C.: taking primary. I'll act as contact and update the incident timeline. If anyone jumps in, please post your name and what access you have.
Priya S.: added runbook pointer to the incident channel and flagged PagerDuty notes. I'll monitor PD for any escalation.
Alex M.: one more — if you need emergency DB access, use the temporary read-replica role, not the master. Avoid write ops unless Priya signs off.
Ben C.: ack. Starting the troubleshooting sequence now. Will update every 5-10m or sooner with changes.
Priya S.: FYI — if you need longer AWS/Grafana access, file a follow-up JIT before expiration. I'll leave a note in the ticket. :thumbsup:
Ben C.: first quick win: restarted 2 consumer pods, consumer lag dropped ~30% in 2m. Monitoring.
SRE Oncall: watching nodes. If lag creeps back, consider temporary throttle on low-priority tenants to buy time (config: `tenant.qos.low=throttle`).
Alex M.: logging out of bridge now. Ben, you have primary. Ping if any escalation. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
